TI Overcoming barriers to eLearning in business education: a qualitative
   study from Uganda
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE eLearning delivery; executive education; digital infrastructure;
   instructor readiness; higher education; eLearning delivery; executive
   education; digital infrastructure; instructor readiness; higher
   education
AB The integration of eLearning in executive business education has expanded globally, offering flexible and scalable learning opportunities for busy professionals. However, in developing contexts like Uganda, the delivery of executive eLearning for business programs faces persistent infrastructural, pedagogical, and contextual challenges. Despite a growing demand for continuous professional development, low internet penetration, limited digital literacy, and insufficient instructional capacity continue to hinder effective implementation. This study investigates the key barriers affecting the delivery of eLearning for executive business programs in Uganda and proposes practical solutions to improve its effectiveness. Guided by a qualitative research design, the study involved in-depth interviews with 20 stakeholders, including program coordinators, instructional designers, and executive business learners (MBA program) from Makerere University Business School (MUBS). Data were analyzed thematically to identify patterns related to technology access, instructor preparedness, and learner engagement. Findings reveal that inadequate digital infrastructure, lack of tailored instructional design, and minimal cultural-contextual adaptation are major obstacles. Additionally, limited training for instructors in digital pedagogy contributes to low interactivity and learner disengagement. The study concludes that overcoming these challenges requires a multipronged strategy involving investment in digital infrastructure, capacity building for facilitators, and contextually adapted eLearning models. These findings have implications for policymakers, academic institutions, and instructional designers seeking to enhance the reach and impact of executive education in low-resource settings.

TI Examining the systematic complexification assumption for expository
   texts in German STEM schoolbooks
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Systematic complexification assumption; language; linguistic features;
   expository texts; STEM education
ID LANGUAGE DEMANDS; SENTENCE LENGTH; COMPREHENSION; MATHEMATICS; WORDS;
   CONNECTIVES; VOCABULARY; COMPLEXITY; FREQUENCY; DIFFICULT
AB An appropriate level of linguistic complexity in schoolbook texts that matches students' reading skills play in important role in STEM-learning. According to the systematic complexification assumption the linguistic complexity should increase across Grade levels. However, only few studies examined this assumption for German STEM expository texts used in school. In the present study we investigated the systematic complexification assumption. For this, we analyzed N = 914 expository texts stemming from biology, geography, and mathematics secondary school schoolbooks regarding 13 (quantitative and qualitative) indicators of linguistic complexity. To test the systematic complexification assumption, multivariate analyses of variance with post-hoc tests were conducted. The results showed that the systematic complexification assumption can mostly be corroborated for all examined STEM subjects, when quantitative linguistic features are considered. However, when looking into qualitative features, the results become less clear. STEM schoolbook authors seem to be aware of surface-level complexity, but greater awareness is needed when it comes to qualitative features. Future studies should corroborate the present findings by examining larger text corpora and extend them to further STEM subjects.

TI Effective practices for reducing underachievement and early school
   leaving: insights from successful learning environments
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Early school leaving; underachievement; vulnerable students; effective
   learning environments
ID LEADERSHIP; EDUCATION
AB Over the past two decades, early school leaving (ESL) rates in the European Union have significantly decreased, from 17.6% in 2000 to 9.5% in 2023. ESL refers to individuals aged 18-24 who leave education without upper secondary qualifications. Ireland has excelled by cutting its ESL rate to 4% in 2023 through initiatives like the Delivering Equality of Opportunity in Schools (DEIS) Plan and TUSLA Education Support Services. These programs address inequities by offering guidance, alternative pathways, and promoting attendance and retention. Despite progress, students from disadvantaged backgrounds, including migrants and Travelers, still face poorer educational outcomes. This research examines inclusive learning environments and their role in improving engagement, retention, and progression. Case studies from two high-performing designated DEIS schools illustrate how strong school leadership fosters effective interventions by building partnerships with families and communities. Applying Bronfenbrenner's ecological systems theory, the study emphasizes the significance of interactions at the microsystem and mesosystem levels, supported by cohesive macro-level policies. The research identifies best practices for reducing inequities and improving outcomes across diverse educational contexts.

DT Article

ID EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE; DISPOSITIONS; RESPONSIBILITY
AB In response to global challenges, such as humanitarian crises, technological disruption and socio-cultural fragmentation, teacher education must move beyond the traditional transmission of pedagogical content. This study introduces the humanizing curriculum model, which integrates ethical reflection on socio-scientific issues (SSI) into instructional practice to cultivate responsibility, moral judgment and critical thinking among pre-service madrasah teachers. Developed through an Educational Design Research (EDR) approach, the model was piloted with 120 pre-service madrasah teachers from three study programs within a faculty of Tarbiyah and teacher training in Surabaya, Indonesia. The model comprises four instructional phases: issue exposure, ethical dialogue, individual reflection and action-oriented response. The results demonstrate enhanced ethical sensitivity and responsible action, particularly among pre-service teachers preparing for madrasah contexts (Islamic schools in Indonesia that integrate religious and general education). These findings highlight the critical role of embedding humanistic and ethical principles in teacher education and affirm ethical reflection grounded in the internalization of religious values as a foundation for transformative pedagogy in effectively addressing the complex demands of 21st-century education.

   members in Saudi universities
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Mindfulness; professional development; faculty members; attention and

   Education; Study of Higher Education; Teaching & Learning
ID TEACHERS
AB This descriptive study investigates whether mindfulness level can predict professional development in university faculty members in Saudi Arabia. It also explores other variables that, while unrelated to mindfulness, can directly influence professional development. Through simple random sampling, 310 faculty members at the King Khalid University, Jeddah University, Hail University, Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University, and Hafr Al-Batin University were included. To align educational frameworks with Vision 2030 objectives focused on quality and innovation, the Ministry of Education should formulate unified policies on integrating mindfulness into professional development programmes for all faculty at Saudi universities.

DT Article

   Bilingualism & Multilingualism; Interdisciplinary Language Studies;
   Language & Education
AB This qualitative study aims to employ the Nominal Group Technique to empower educators by identifying and prioritizing pedagogical strategies that optimize the educational development of MA and PhD English language students, grounded in established educational theories such as those of Vygotsky, Bruner and Bandura. A panel of nine experienced university professors and English language experts, all holding doctoral degrees, participated in ten structured NGT sessions to identify, discuss, and prioritize strategies based on expert consensus. To recruit these specialists, a targeted non-random sampling method, along with a snowball sampling technique, was employed. These findings can inform strategic improvements in postgraduate language education and educator development.

TI The effect of decentralised educational decisions on learning
   achievements in secondary schools in selected local government
   authorities in Simiyu region, Tanzania
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Decentralised educational decisions; learning achievement; secondary
   schools; local government authorities; Simiyu region; Tanzania
ID FISCAL DECENTRALIZATION; OUTCOMES
AB A shift in the management of secondary education from the Ministry of Education to local governments in Tanzania has necessitated the endorsement and implementation of local policies to improve schools. However, the impact of such policies on learning outcomes remains uncertain. This study examines the effect of decentralised educational decisions on enhancing learning achievement in the Certificate of Secondary Education Examination (CSEE) across selected districts in the Simiyu region. A quantitative research approach using time series cross-sectional design yielded panel data spanning 2017-2021. Multilevel sampling strategies enabled a random selection of districts and schools, resulting in a final sample of 9634 students who sat for the CSEE over the period under study. Checklists facilitated data collection from school records and national surveys documenting school data. Generalised least squares regression analysis using a random effects model, yielded the study's findings. The results demonstrate that all domains of decentralised educational decisions positively influence learning achievement. Although there are marginally higher learning achievements in boarding and urban schools, the effects of decentralised educational decisions are more pronounced in day and rural schools. These findings underscore the importance of contextual factors when determining local policies to improve schools.

TI Academic resilience mediating perceived academic support and achievement
   in first-year university students
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Academic achievement; academic resilience; perceived academic support;
   perceived family support; perceived peer support; perceived teacher
   support
ID SOCIAL SUPPORT; SUCCESS
AB This study examined the mediating role of academic resilience in the relationship between perceived academic support from family, peers, and teachers and academic achievement among first-year undergraduate students at Ijabara University. Drawing on stress and coping theory and resilience theory, it addresses a critical gap in understanding how these protective factors enhance academic achievement during a critical transitional period. Data were collected using established scales, the Perceived Academic Support Scale (Guti & eacute;rrez et al., 2017) and Cassidy's (2016) Academic Resilience Scale (validated by Cui et al., 2023). Participants were selected via a stratified random sampling method, yielding a pilot sample of 200 students (158 male, 42 female) and a main sample of 503 students (403 male, 100 female). Pearson correlation analyses revealed significant positive associations among perceived academic support, resilience, and achievement (p < 0.05). Structural equation modeling (SEM) demonstrated that academic resilience fully mediated the relationship between family and teacher support and achievement, explaining 39% of the variance in academic outcomes, a significant contribution to understanding student success. The absence of indirect effects from peer support aligns with cultural expectations in Ethiopia's collectivist, high-power-distance society, where family and teacher roles are prioritized over less structured peer networks. These findings underscore resilience as a critical mechanism, offering practical implications for designing resilience-building interventions to enhance student success. Limitations include gender imbalance, cross-sectional design, and a single-university focus, suggesting future longitudinal and multi-institutional research to enhance generalizability.

   concept instruction; pedagogical content knowledge; qualitative

AB This qualitative study investigates how Foundation Phase teachers' professional identities influence their approaches to teaching number concepts. Twelve teachers from Johannesburg East District were purposively selected to participate. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations, and analysed thematically. Findings suggest that a strong, positive professional identity is closely linked to effective pedagogical practices. Teachers who viewed themselves as knowledgeable and nurturing-often adopting an in loco parentis role-demonstrated high levels of motivation, confidence, and relational warmth in their teaching. These educators were deeply committed to helping young learners grasp number concepts. In contrast, teachers whose professional identities were more aligned with administrative or social work roles often experienced role ambiguity and systemic pressures, which disrupted their instructional coherence. This misalignment between self-concept and classroom practice led to fragmented teaching and difficulty integrating core pedagogical principles. The study concludes that teachers' self-perceptions significantly shape their instructional choices and effectiveness in mathematics education. It recommends that educational authorities prioritise ongoing professional development that not only enhances teaching competence but also fosters a coherent and positive professional identity among Foundation Phase teachers.

TI Tailoring inquiry for young scientists: investigating the impact of a DI
   PBL model on elementary students' curiosity in biodiversity learning
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Biodiversity lesson; curiosity; differentiated instruction; elementary
   science; problem-based learning; Social Sciences; Education; Early
   Years; Development Studies, Environment, Social Work, Urban Studies;
   Sociology
ID IMPLEMENTATION; PRINCIPLES; TEACHERS
AB This study examined the impact of a Differentiated Instruction-Problem-Based Learning (DI-PBL) model on elementary students' curiosity in biodiversity lessons. Using a quasi-experimental design, two intact classes of fifth-grade students (n = 44) were assigned to experimental and control groups. Data were collected through a 26-item curiosity questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results showed that the DI-PBL model significantly enhanced students' curiosity compared to traditional instruction. The model demonstrated strong explanatory power (R2 = 0.739), indicating that 73.9% of the variance in curiosity was explained by the five instructional stages. Among these, Guiding Group and Individual Investigations (beta = 0.619) made the strongest contribution, while Developing and Presenting Work had minimal direct influence (beta = 0.031). These findings highlight that curiosity is most effectively stimulated during early and inquiry-focused stages of the DI-PBL process. Practically, this study suggests that teachers can foster curiosity by tailoring inquiry activities to students' learning profiles and emphasizing investigation and exploration. Differentiated strategies such as visual aids, peer discussion, and hands-on tasks can make inquiry more accessible and engaging. Beyond science learning, the DI-PBL framework offers a promising approach for cultivating curiosity as a transferable learning disposition across school subjects.

TI From performance standards to evidence-based decisions: applying
   self-starting control charts in higher education program assessment
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Higher education; program assessment; statistical process control
AB This study demonstrates that self-starting control charts for program-level assessment in higher education provide improved decision support over the use of fixed performance standards. Using a 5-year case study of program outcome assessment data, self-starting control charts yielded more accurate and actionable interpretations in 34% of observations when compared to the use of fixed performance standards. The advantages of self-starting control charts include their ability to detect true changes in student achievement levels; monitor outcomes achieved at both high and low levels, and remain effective as programs evolve. The Q-chart self-starting statistical process control (SPC) methodology presented offers a flexible and statistically valid approach applicable to various types of assessment methods and data sources in program-level evaluation. Q-charts are readily implementable with common software such as spreadsheets. The implications of adopting this approach include improved efficiency in the use of resources, increased program outcome achievement, and statistically sound continuous improvement documentation.

TI Cracking the math code: the impact of flipped classroom on
   problem-solving, digital fluency and self-directed learning
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Flipped classroom; math problem-solving; digital literacy; self-directed
   learning; active learning; higher education
AB Flipped Learning (FL) has gained significant traction in both theoretical research and practical application across various educational levels, fostering active discourse among scholars and practitioners. While some students face challenges related to technological access, the increasing availability of digital tools, educational resources and internet connectivity has facilitated the broader adoption of FL pedagogical approaches. As education shifts toward technology-enhanced, student-centered learning, the flipped classroom emerges as a viable alternative to traditional instruction. This study explores the impact of the flipped classroom model on problem-solving skills, digital literacy and self-directed learning (SDL) among undergraduate mathematics students. Employing a mixed-methods design, the study involved 200 undergraduate students at Kuwait University. Data collection included pre- and post-intervention assessments, surveys and semi-structured interviews. Quantitative findings revealed significant improvements in problem-solving skills (p < 0.05) and digital literacy (p < 0.05), whereas SDL showed no statistically significant change. Although SDL did not reveal any statistically significant changes, this could be attributed to the intervention's focus on organized collaboration, which favored directed problem-solving rather than explicit instruction in metacognitive strategies. Qualitative data highlighted increased engagement, autonomy and critical thinking. These results support the flipped classroom as an effective approach to modernizing mathematics education, aligning with global trends in digital transformation.

TI Assessing translation quality of promotional tourist texts: a case study
   of VisitSaudi website
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Translation; text analysis; tourism promotion; translation quality
   assessment; VisitSaudi; website analysis
AB This study assesses the translation quality of website tourism promotional texts (TPTs) by examining the transfer of Arabic high-context cultural elements into English low context culture. The study developed a conceptual framework for translation quality assessment (TQA)of TPTs with of linguistic, cultural and website promotional dimensions. In this case study, we collected the available promotional texts (34texts) from the genre of Culture and History on the VisitSaudi website forming a corpus of more than ten thousand words for Arabic-English versions. The data was then analyzed quantitatively and qualitatively against a rubric developed and validated based on the conceptual framework. The study revealed that the translated texts were linguistically of moderate quality in terms of accuracy, clarity and naturalness(2.06 out of3). As for the cultural quality, most of the translated texts coped with the English low context culture with some ideological discrepancies in traditional texts. For website promotional quality, the translators employed persuasive language in 70% of the texts. More han half of the texts (55%) conveyed the intended promotional messages to the target audience. The website displays photos for each text (100%) which promotes the tourist's appeal. The website is also found to be user-unfriendly for visitors to write their comments. The study offers some practical implications for tourism website practitioners.

TI Primary classroom rules in Confucian heritage culture-a case study in
   Vietnam
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Classroom rules; primary schools; Confucian heritage; primary students;
   Vietnam; Psychological Science; Classroom Practice; Educational
   Psychology
ID EDUCATION
AB The establishment of classroom rules is fundamental to effective class management, serving as a framework that facilitates order and discipline within the educational environment. Developing a system of regulations tailored to the developmental needs of primary school students not only fosters student discipline but also alleviates the workload of teachers. In Vietnam, where Confucianism exerts a profound cultural influence, classroom rules often reflect Confucian disciplinary principles. Data for this study were collected through questionnaires and interviews with teachers and parents from Vietnamese primary schools. The findings indicate that both teachers and parents acknowledge the importance of classroom rules in shaping student behavior. However, due to the hierarchical nature of Confucian values, the implementation of these rules tends to follow a top-down approach, with students primarily tasked with compliance rather than participation in rule creation. This Confucian heritage significantly shapes disciplinary practices, underscoring the need for these principles to be maintained while also advocating for a more collaborative process of rule formation between teachers and students.

   links with attitudes, activity, and self-concept in Welsh adolescents
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article

   Social Sciences, Physical Activity and Health; Sport and Exercise
   Science; Social Sciences, Secondary Physical Education; Social Sciences
ID CARDIORESPIRATORY FITNESS; PERCEPTION PROFILE; CHILDREN; HEALTH; SCALE
AB This study investigated enjoyment levels in physical education (PE) among adolescent students in their first year of secondary school in Wales (UK), examining associations with attitudes toward PE, physical self-perceptions, enjoyment of physical activity (PA), and PA behaviours. Participants were 192 Year 7 pupils (102 boys, 90 girls; M age = 12.31 years) from three secondary schools in South-East Wales. Students completed validated questionnaires assessing PE enjoyment (FIPE), PA enjoyment (PACES), PA behaviour (PAQ-A), physical self-perceptions (CY-PSPP), and attitudes toward PE (PEAAS). TI When coping becomes sacred: positive and negative religious coping in
   the link between school stress, bullying, and student mental health
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE School stress; bullying experiences; positive religious coping; negative
   religious coping; mental health; adolescence; age; gender; General
   Psychology; Educational Psychology; Mental Health; Secondary Education;
   Education - Social Sciences; Religion
ID PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS; EMOTION REGULATION; EARLY ADOLESCENCE;
   VICTIMIZATION; METAANALYSIS; IMPACT; PSYCHOPATHOLOGY; PREVALENCE;
   ADJUSTMENT; STRATEGIES
AB Religious coping, encompassing both positive and negative dimensions, is frequently associated with mental health outcomes when individuals face stressful life events. In the school context, students frequently encounter various sources of stress, including academic demands and peer-related challenges. Bullying remains one of the most prevalent and harmful experiences among students, emerging as a global issue that significantly affects their mental health. School stress and bullying experiences can therefore be viewed as interrelated stressors that threaten students' mental health. This study aimed to examine the mediating roles of positive and negative religious coping in the relationship between school stress, bullying experiences, and students' mental health, while statistically controlling for age and gender. Data were collected through a face-to-face survey using self-administered questionnaires among secondary school students in Bandung, Indonesia (n = 310). The results revealed that negative religious coping significantly worsened students' mental health, particularly under high school stress, whereas positive religious coping showed a weak but non-significant protective tendency. Bullying experiences did not significantly moderate these relationships, suggesting that coping mechanisms may operate similarly across varying levels of peer victimization. These findings highlight the importance of developing interventions that strengthen adaptive religious coping strategies and address maladaptive beliefs to promote better mental health among adolescents.

   push-pull; consumer value; international students; marketing; Social
   Sciences; Higher Education; International Student Mobility;
   Internationalization
ID HIGHER-EDUCATION; ABROAD; CHOICE; CHINA; EXPLORATION; CHALLENGES;
   MOBILITY
AB This research aims to offer an integrative picture of contemporary international student flows into Asian higher education (HE) destinations. It undertakes a year-on-year analysis of the UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS) dataset of the recent 2013-2022/23 timeline to quantify and compare shifts in student mobility to four regions and eight countries. The findings reveal (i) the remarkable upsurge in inbound mobility pertaining to the 'Western Asia' region, buoyed mainly by the fourfold increase in student mobility to Turkey and the UAE, (ii) the steady increase in international student flows to frontrunners China and Japan and (iii) the perceptible international student source region multipolarity in several Asian receiving countries. Empirical studies examining the push-pull dynamics in major Asian destinations are reviewed and then synthesised into a configuration of consumption values, namely, conditional, social, emotional and functional (quality/performance and price/value) to gain a consumer purchase behaviour standpoint. Such a synthesis is an effort to go beyond the linear set of external (macro-focused) factors accentuated in westward mobility-led choice models.

TI From sorogan to digital learning: a systematic literature network
   analysis of pesantren learning models
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Pesantren; Islamic boarding school; learning models; character
   education; Systematic Literature Network Analysis; Pesantren; Islamic
   boarding school; learning models; character education; Systematic
   Literature Network Analysis
ID EDUCATION
AB This study examines the evolution of learning models in Indonesian pesantren from 2007 to 2025 using a Systematic Literature Network Analysis (SLNA) based on Scopus-indexed publications. The research aims to identify major trends and factors shaping the transformation of pesantren education as it balances traditional Islamic pedagogy with contemporary, technology-enhanced learning approaches. Employing a mixed bibliometric and systematic review methodology within the PRISMA framework, the study analyzed 86 peer-reviewed articles through citation, co-authorship, and co-word analyses using VOSviewer. The results reveal a progressive shift from classical methods such as Sorogan and Bandongan toward hybrid and digital-based models emphasizing inclusivity, character education, and technological literacy. While pesantren continue to preserve their religious and cultural integrity, they increasingly integrate digital tools to address globalization and modern educational demands. Key challenges include balancing heritage with innovation, infrastructural disparities, and uneven digital adoption. This study contributes a longitudinal understanding of pesantren's pedagogical transformation, offering theoretical and practical insights for policymakers and educators. Despite limitations related to database scope, the integration of bibliometric and systematic approaches in this SLNA provides a robust analytical framework for examining complex educational shifts within Islamic learning institutions.

TI Home-schooling and parent-child relationships during lockdown in
   England: a Foucauldian discourse analysis
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Home-schooling; Covid; lockdown; parent-child relationships; Foucauldian
   discourse analysis; Social sciences; Education; Education policy and
   politics; Education policy; Curriculum; Pedagogy; Technology;
   Engineering and technology
ID SELF-EFFICACY
AB The aim of this study was to explore and describe the impact of home-schooling during the Covid-19 lockdown on parent-child relationships. Online semi-structured interviews were conducted with an opportunistic sample of parents (n = 11) in England who were experiencing home-schooling during the first period of lockdown. A Foucauldian Discourse Analysis was conducted on the data and six subject positions were revealed. Home-schooling was variously constructed as a bonding experience, an opportunity for new appreciation of children, the cause of new conflicts in the home setting, the cause of psychological stress, the creation of a new parent-teacher role and the creation of a new child-pupil role. These discursive constructions confirmed the findings of previous research into lockdown home-schooling related to the conflicts of time and space, the impact of differing levels of parental self-efficacy, and direction of children's development. This research provided further detailed descriptions of the lived experiences of participants in these areas but also supported recent research on parental attachment that suggests that the construction of parent-child relationships can be quickly re-negotiated under the influence of external factors.

TI The GLASS tool: a new lens for evaluating generalist leadership
   competencies for medical education
SO MEDICAL EDUCATION ONLINE
LA English
DT Article
DE Medical education; competencies; course directors; generalist; health
   professions education; integrated curriculum; GLASS; leadership;
   longitudinal courses
ID DELPHI
AB Recent shifts in medical education have moved curricula away from siloed, discipline-based courses toward competency-focused, integrated models. Leading within a longitudinal, integrated curriculum requires a distinct set of leadership competencies. To address this need, medical education leaders across five institutions collaborated to develop a generalist leadership framework. Using a modified Delphi process, the team conducted literature reviews reviewing both published and gray literature and held monthly meetings over six months. This process resulted in the identification of core competencies, organized into three domains: Humility and Life-long Learning, Supporting Diverse Collaborations, and Holistic Stewardship of the Curriculum. A competency based self-assessment tool, Generalist Leadership Assessment for Skills and Strengths (GLASS) Tool, was then developed around this framework. The GLASS tool was piloted and validated in workshops at three national medical education conferences. Feedback from these sessions demonstrated strong support for the tool, with an average of 94% agreement on the relevance and clarity of the competencies. Participants used the tool to self-assess their leadership competencies, with higher self-ratings observed in the domain of humility and life-long learning over holistic stewardship of the curriculum. The tool was refined based on expert input clarifying the milestones and consolidating the competencies. The GLASS tool is designed to support reflective leadership development across four levels of educational engagement: individual, departmental, institutional, and national. It offers a transparent approach for faculty development, leadership readiness, and strategic planning in evolving medical education environments.

TI Understanding academic well-being in indigenous contexts: a predictive
   analysis of social support and cultural diversity among senior high
   school indigenous students in Caraga
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Students' backgrounds; indigenous families; perceived social support;
   well-being; students; Multicultural Education; Anthropology - Soc Sci;
   Education - Social Sciences
AB The paper explored the predictors of the academic well-being of Indigenous students, focusing on perceived social support from families and friends and their diverse backgrounds. It assessed well-being across cognitive, psychological, social, physical, and material dimensions for students from poverty-stricken families. Using a descriptive-predictive design, specifically the weighted mean, and multiple regression analysis, the study targeted senior high students from Surigao del Norte Manobos, Agusan del Norte Higaonons, and Agusan del Sur Banwaons. Slovin's Formula determined the sample size, and simple random sampling selected 201 respondents. Data were collected using an adapted OECD How's Life Framework questionnaire. Findings revealed significant disparities in material resources based on ethnicity and income, impacting academic performance. Multiple regression analysis showed that Indigenous family support significantly influences overall well-being. The study recommended collaborative efforts among parents, schools, and the government to ensure equal educational opportunities and resources for all students. Policy recommendations were crafted to guide educational institutions in making curricular changes to better support students' needs. Future researchers may develop culturally specific measurement tools in collaboration with Indigenous communities that can capture unique cultural contexts as this is identified as the study's limitation.

TI MOOC-virtual simulation integration enhances surgical clinical skills: a
   quasi-experimental study
SO MEDICAL EDUCATION ONLINE
LA English
DT Article
DE Medical education; virtual simulation experiment; MOOC; general surgery
   experiment; teaching model
ID STUDENTS
AB This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a teaching model combining massive open online course (MOOC) with virtual simulation experiments on clinical skills training. A quasi-experimental design was employed in the Second Clinical College of Wuhan University. The control group received traditional face-to-face teaching, while the experimental group received a teaching model combining MOOC instruction with virtual simulation experiments. After completing the course, both groups participated in a theoretical test and a Structured Clinical Skills Assessment to assess their mastery of clinical skills. Additionally, a questionnaire survey was conducted to assess the effectiveness of the experimental teaching model and to gauge student satisfaction. The experimental group's theoretical test scores were significantly higher than those of the control group, and the experimental group's Structured Clinical Skills Assessment scores were significantly higher than those of the control group, with statistically significant differences (p < 0.05). The post-course questionnaire survey of the experimental group showed that most students were satisfied with the teaching model. In the general surgery experiment course, the teaching model combining MOOC instruction with virtual simulation experiments is an effective teaching method that improves surgical skill performance and increases student satisfaction.

TI Coding, creativity, and competence: preservice teachers' learning
   through an online scratch club
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Coding; preservice teacher education; guided play; creativity; online
   learning; Science of learning
ID GUIDED PLAY
AB This study explored the experiences of three cohorts of preservice teachers who participated in an extracurricular online Scratch Coding Club (SCC). We were interested in exploring whether our assumption was valid that involvement in the SCC would enrich preservice teachers' preparation for teaching (from their perspectives) and, if so, in what ways. The SCC's goal was to develop key competencies like creative and critical thinking, collaboration, communication, computational thinking and digital fluency - skills essential for both teaching and the modern workforce. The club further offers hands-on, playful coding experiences, demonstrating how Scratch can foster creativity and positive emotions in the classroom. A qualitative interpretive research approach was adopted for this study due to the interest in how the individuals involved (the preservice teachers) made sense and meaning of their involvement with the SCC. The study revealed three main findings; firstly, preservice teachers valued the development of competencies, especially creativity; secondly, they gained valuable insights into teaching, particularly by using Scratch to enrich lessons; and lastly, their personal dispositions and life skills were enhanced.

TI Comparing teaching actions in face-to-face and synchronous online
   settings using an observation protocol for K-12 education
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Quality of online teaching; K-12 online synchronous teaching;
   communities of inquiry; structured class observation; online teaching
   activities; Quality of online teaching; K-12 online synchronous
   teaching; communities of inquiry; structured class observation; online
   teaching activities
ID TEACHERS; COMPETENCES; AGREEMENT; QUALITY; COURSES; SKILLS
AB Synchronous online education became crucial during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, more research needs to be done on how to observe the quality of synchronous online teaching in K-12. This research seeks to address this gap by comparing the activities that teachers engage in during synchronous online classes with those used in face-to-face scenarios to adapt a face-to-face observation protocol to be used in both situations. Quantitative and qualitative techniques were used to compare classroom observations of teachers performing similar lessons in the two scenarios. Results show that teachers working online engaged in more actions associated with classroom management but fewer related to promoting cooperation, assessment, and offering feedback to their students. The qualitative results complement these findings, showing that evaluating the quality of teaching in synchronous online teaching settings requires additional indicators tailored to its unique characteristics. Based on this, we propose a set of indicators to observe online synchronous teaching quality. These findings can inform in-service teachers, professional development courses, and further research efforts.

TI Opportunities, benefits and challenges of implementing preschool
   education in Ethiopia
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Caregivers; challenges; early childhood care and education;
   opportunities; preschool
ID EARLY-CHILDHOOD EDUCATION; SUPPORT
AB Preschool or Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) prepares children for formal education, creating a strong and wide basis for lifelong learning and well-being. Thus, the present investigation investigated the available opportunities, advantages, and challenges of implementing preschool education in Ethiopia's Amhara regional state. For achieving this purpose, a case study design was used with forty people, providing qualitative data. As a result, the startup of ECCE in government schools, the availability of ECCE policy and the positive attitudes of the children, community and parents found opportunities for implementing ECCE. Through ECCE, children can benefit from exploring their surrounding environment, sharing social life and reducing dropout rates. However, the implementation of ECCE was challenged by poor policy implementation, weak institutional collaboration, inadequate teaching and learning resources, lack of infrastructures, developmentally inappropriate education curriculum and deficiency of proper professional development of teachers and caregivers. The study's findings have significant implications for the advancement of the preschool program by informing policymakers and educators about opportunities, benefits and challenges of implementing ECCE, which result in improving early childhood learning environments, improving teacher training, and better allocating resources to support children's developmental needs and achieving Sustainable Development Goal-4 (quality education).

TI Analysis and prospect of 'Chinese Educational Modernization Policy': a
   textual study based on 155 policy documents
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Education modernization; policy analysis; text mining; Chinese
   education; digital transformation; Education modernization; policy
   analysis; text mining; Chinese education; digital transformation
AB Education modernization is the core issue of China's education reform and development, which have received significant attention in the aspects of policy formulation, academic research and practical exploration in recent years. This study analyzes 155 policy documents related to the Chinese Educational Modernization Policy, employing a content analysis methodology. The utilizing tools such as NVivo 11.0 Plus, ROSTCM6, and Microsoft Word cloud applications, it conducts word frequency statistics, topic correlation assessments, and cluster analyses of the policy texts. The research systematically elucidates the key areas and developmental directions of 'Chinese Educational Modernization Policy'. The findings indicate that this modernization initiative emphasizes five critical dimensions: (1) human modernization and institutional innovation (two-wheel drive); (2) Social collaboration and innovation mechanism; (3) Systematic construction of education support system; (4) Integration of theoretical construction and practical paths; (5) Multi-dimensional coordinated development system. Based on the findings, this study proposes four key policy recommendations: (1) establishing a hierarchical teacher training system; (2) developing a localized four-spiral collaboration mechanism for innovative talent cultivation; (3) implementing a phased strategy for educational digital transformation; (4) creating a multi-dimensional safeguard mechanism to ensure policy implementation. Therefore, these findings not only provide a theoretical basis for the in-depth promotion of China's education modernization but also offer a valuable reference for global education development, especially for developing countries to explore localized education modernization models.

TI Self-regulated learning among higher education economics students: does
   gender and academic level matter?
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Academic level; economics students; gender; higher education;
   self-regulated learning; Study Skills; Theories of Learning; Educational
   Psychology; Higher Education; Education - Social Sciences
ID EFFICACY; VALIDITY; BELIEFS
AB Self-regulated learning (SRL) plays a pivotal role in Economics education at the higher education (HE) level, enabling students to manage their cognitive processes, strategies, and motivations for deeper understanding, critical thinking, and effective application of economic concepts across contexts. This study examined SRL among HE Economics students in Ghana, focusing on potential differences across gender and academic levels. Employing a cross-sectional survey design and the census method, data were collected from 452 students using an adapted self-regulated learning scale. Descriptive statistics (means and standard deviations) and two-way multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) were used for analysis. Findings indicated a generally high level of SRL among students, highlighting the relevance of promoting self-directed learning behaviours in HE. However, no statistically significant differences emerged in SRL across gender or academic level. The study recommends the integration of SRL strategies into Economics curricula to foster learner autonomy and enhance academic outcomes. Furthermore, educators and policymakers are urged to create supportive environments that nurture self-regulatory skills among students, irrespective of gender or academic level. Such efforts will better equip Economics students to adapt and excel in the dynamic landscape of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR).

TI Sixth graders' reading comprehension: English for young learners
   proficiency analysis and implication
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Reading comprehension; English acquisition; young learners; gender;
   PLS-SEM; Reading comprehension; English acquisition; young learners;
   gender; PLS-SEM
ID LITERACY; LANGUAGE; TEXT
AB Reading comprehension (RC) is a critical component of English acquisition (EA), yet the role of gender in this relationship remains underexplored in the Indonesian context. This study investigates the contribution of RC to EA among sixth-grade students, considering gender as a moderating factor. Data were obtained from 84 students through 18 informal comprehension assessments and six teacher-designed English proficiency evaluations. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was applied to analyze the relationships among RC categories-literal, inferential, and critical comprehension. The RC construct demonstrated high reliability (Cronbach's Alpha = 0.882; Composite Reliability = 0.923; AVE = 0.801). RC positively correlated with EA (HTMT = 0.333), with literal comprehension achieving the highest mean (X<overline> = 36.15) and critical comprehension the lowest (X<overline> = 14.67). RC significantly predicted EA (beta = 0.279), explaining 27.9% of the variance (p = 0.007). Gender analysis revealed stronger effects of RC on EA among boys (beta = 0.424), while the relationship was weaker and statistically insignificant among girls (beta = -0.354). Findings highlight the importance of implementing gender-responsive instructional strategies that go beyond word recognition, strengthen higher-order comprehension skills, and promote equitable English acquisition.

TI The relationship between teachers' knowledge and learners' performance
   in physical sciences from selected schools of Lejweleputswa district
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE pedagogical content knowledge; content knowledge; teacher knowledge;
   pedagogical knowledge; physical sciences; learner performance;
   pedagogical content knowledge; content knowledge; teacher knowledge;
   pedagogical knowledge; physical sciences; learner performance
AB The purpose of the study was to determine the relationship between Physical Sciences educators' content knowledge and the learners' performance. The study employed a survey design with a sample of 41 teachers from 15 schools in the Lejweleputswa District of the Free State Province. A questionnaire was used to collect data, which was analyzed using descriptive statistics and the Chi-square test in SPSS. The Chi-square test serves as a statistical method for assessing the relationship between two categorical variables, which in this study are different teachers' knowledge and learners' performance. The overall results show that teachers' Pedagogical Content Knowledge did not have a direct relationship with learners' performance in all four years of study. However, the scientific knowledge of the Physical Sciences educators shows a relationship with learners' performance over four years (p < 0.05). The absence of a relationship between teachers' Pedagogical Content Knowledge and learners' performance suggests that other factors impacted learners' performance, as schools that participated in the study did not perform better in national examinations than those that did not. These findings have implications for schools where the teachers' knowledge is expected to improve the quality of education.

TI Idiographic self-regulated affordance uptake in AI-mediated language
   learning
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Affordances; artificial intelligence; self-regulated; idiographic study;
   complexity; ecological approach
AB Research on AI-mediated language learning has often emphasized aggregate measures of performance and engagement, yet little is known about how learners individually perceive and enact affordances in sustained interaction with conversational agents. This study addressed this gap through an idiographic multiple-case analysis of four Vietnamese adults who engaged in eight sessions of self-directed English practice with ChatGPT. Interaction logs and stimulated recall interviews were analyzed using a five-dimensional affordance framework consisting of perceptibility, valence, intentionality, compositionality, and normativity to trace how uptake unfolded across time. The findings show that each learner developed a distinct trajectory. Some orchestrated affordances proactively and in compositional ways, others constrained uptake through cautious or normative orientations and shifts in affect, often triggering turning points in how action potentials were noticed and realized. These results demonstrate that affordances are not static features of AI systems but emergent relations that acquire significance only in action and ecologically. The study advances affordance theory in language education by showing that variability is not incidental but constitutive of learning ecologies, and it suggests that effective AI-mediated pedagogy requires preparing learners to notice, revalue, and creatively combine affordances in ways that support autonomy and sustained engagement.

   environment scale in mathematics
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Authentic learning; learning context; learning environment; situated
   learning; mathematics learning; Educational Psychology;
   Primary/Elementary Education
ID DESIGN
AB Learner-oriented instances reflecting real-world situations mainly authentic learning contexts are necessary for realistic mathematics. The study aimed at conceptualizing authenticity of learning and establishing a scale to evaluate authenticity of learning by students and investigating underlying structures. Researchers employed an exploratory mixed-methods design. Comprehensive conceptualization was made with the aid of extensive literature reviews. Thorough literature review was made and the researchers investigated ten dimensions using content analysis. Based on the fit indices the model was accepted implying stability. The current findings can contribute for policymakers, administrators, parents, researchers, and teachers to clarifying the concept authentic learning environment and designing and evaluating learning environment in mathematics.

TI Evaluating the effectiveness of Nearpod's interactive science modules on
   student achievement in Saudi middle schools
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Interactive technology; science education; Nearpod; student achievement;
   Interactive technology; science education; Nearpod; Academic
   performance; student achievement
ID PHET SIMULATIONS; EDUCATION
AB Implementing interactive technology in science education allows students who are not easily engaged to engage, motivates them, and improves their academic performance. The digital science modules offered by Nearpod in Saudi Arabian middle schools introduce an option to modernize teaching and conform to the changes in the educational goals and approaches nationally. The study involved 15 students as interveners, consisting of different students in different schools of Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, to implement a 3-week intervention with the availability of interactive solutions offered by Nearpod quizzes, simulations, collaborative boards, and immediate feedback to learn fundamental concepts in science. The pre- and post-tests showed an average increase in scores of 23 points, showing a drastic concept increase. There were high engagement metrics, with students having finished over five modules and making an average of more than 30 interactions. Perception surveys indicated a high degree of approval, with the average rating in understanding, enjoyment, and involvement above 4.1 points. Despite encouraging results, generalizability is limited by the small exploratory sample size (n = 15) and absence of a control group. Larger, representative cohorts are required for future research. There was a slight negative correlation (r = -0.15) between the levels of engagement and the score improvement, which means that the higher levels of activity did not always lead to higher levels of achievement. This observation reminds us of differentiated instruction's significance and progressive feedback's design. Nearpod showed promise of academic and experiential advantages in Saudi middle school science lessons, but the tiny, experimental sample should guide interpretation.

TI Gender and regional differences in physical education teachers'
   perspectives on basketball instruction in Slovakia
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Physical education; basketball; Slovakia; gender differences; urban vs.
   rural schools; teaching practices; Social Sciences; Education; Adult
   Education and Lifelong Learning; Work-based Learning; Philosophy of
   Education; Research Methods in Education
ID MOTOR ABILITIES
AB Basketball is a central component of physical education in Slovak schools, contributing to students' physical, cognitive and social development. The success of basketball instruction largely depends on the competencies, experiences and attitudes of physical education (PE) teachers. This study explores Slovak PE teachers' opinions, practices and challenges related to basketball teaching. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 1168 PE teachers (635 men and 533 women) from 635 schools during the 2023/2024 academic year. Significant gender-based and regional differences were identified. Male teachers favored sports games, particularly football and applied technical teaching approaches more often, while female teachers preferred gymnastics, volleyball and game-oriented strategies. Urban teachers expressed more favorable attitudes toward basketball, taught it more frequently and reported better equipment availability compared to rural teachers. However, all groups cited limited time and low interest in teaching basketball as common shortcomings. Basketball instruction in Slovak schools is shaped by both teacher gender and school setting. These findings underscore the need for targeted professional development, enhanced infrastructure and curriculum reform to ensure equitable and effective basketball education. By addressing these factors, the study provides a foundation for improving teaching practices and supporting more inclusive PE across diverse school contexts.

TI Reform and practice of the interdisciplinary competency cultivation
   model based on the German economic engineering talent training
SO COGENT EDUCATION

DT Article

AB Engineering talent cultivation requires a balance of systemic knowledge, interdisciplinary understanding, and practicality skills. German economic engineering programs, centered on a 'technology-science-humanities' training model, have successfully shaped versatile engineering talents. By recognizing the deficiency in humanities and social sciences literacy-particularly in economics and management knowledge-among domestic engineering students, an interdisciplinary 'Engineering + Economics/Management' project-based curriculum has been introduced in Chinese-German Institute for Applied Engineering of Zhejiang University of Science and Technology, in which the German economic engineering training model was adopted. The annual high-quality employment rate for graduates reached approximately 40.3%, far exceeding the university's average level. The institute's successful experience can serve as a valuable reference for cultivating humanities and social sciences literacy in engineering education in China.

TI Perceptions of social inclusion among secondary school teachers in
   Bangladesh
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Inclusive education; secondary education; secondary teachers; social
   inclusion; special education; Social Sciences; Education; Behavioral
   Sciences; Educational Psychology; Cognitive Psychology; Motivation
AB Social inclusion in the classroom can be a vital practice in order to ensure Education for All (EFA) . The study aimed to explore effective knowledge and practices of secondary schools teachers in various geographical regions of Bangladesh. Qualitative research was employed where researchers conducted semi-structured interviews to get insightful data on 50 teachers in secondary schools around Dhaka city, teaching grades VI to X and 10 secondary education monitoring officers. Interpretation of the obtained data was carried out using thematic analysis. Results indicated that the social inclusion practices had formal conceptual grounding among the teachers, yet they had limited knowledge of this. Consequently, the concept of social inclusion was more of a hypothetical term as it was written in documents rather than practiced in classroom. The current study underlines the importance of profession-specific professional development to improve teachers' knowledge about social inclusion. It proposes the initiative of the pre-service as well as in-service training to allow the teachers to be respectful of learner differences. These would enhance the regulation of teaching and assessment procedures, foster the development of a positive learning environment, and ultimately lead to improved performance among students. Also, the research recommends better deployment of resources to facilitate greater inclusion in the learning process in the secondary schools in Bangladesh.

TI Effects of task repetition awareness and the need for cognition on the
   complexity, accuracy, and fluency of L2 oral performance
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Task-based language teaching; task repetition; need for cognition;
   complexity; accuracy; fluency; Arts & Humanities; Language & Literature;
   Language & Linguistics; Sociolinguistics; Bilingualism &
   Multilingualism; Interdisciplinary Language Studies; Language &
   Education
AB This study sought to examine whether task repetition awareness and learners' need for cognition as an individual difference have any effects on the complexity, accuracy and fluency of EFL learners' L2 oral productions. Sixty Iranian intermediate EFL learners were randomly selected and assigned to three groups, namely aware group (AG, n = 20), unaware group (UG, n = 20) and, control group (CG, n = 20). The first group required to perform a problem-solving task and after completion, they were instructed the benefits of repeating a task. This group was asked to repeat the exact task for another three times. Meanwhile, the task was introduced to the unaware group and this time, they repeated the task three times after the first task completion, without the awareness The control group only participated in the first task performance and final stage of performance. The oral performance wasanalyzed based on the accuracy, fluency, and complexity measures. At the final session, all three groups answered the need for cognition questionnaire. The results of MANOVA analysis indicated that task repetition awareness increases the complexity of oral productions of EFL learners. In addition, task repetition alone is helpful in increasing the fluency of the participants. The results of need for cognition were not significant in this study. Implications for further research and language teachers are also provided.

TI Predictive value of prior academic and psychosocial factors on
   first-year students' academic achievement at Wallaga University
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Academic achievement; prior academic performance; academic adjustment;
   psychosocial factors
ID SELF-ESTEEM; SOCIAL SUPPORT; MEDICAL-STUDENTS; COLLEGE; PERFORMANCE;
   ADJUSTMENT; SUCCESS; STRESS; SCHOOL; 1ST
AB This study aims to determine to what extent prior academic performance (secondary school Grade Point Average (GPA) and Ethiopian University Entrance Exam (EUEE) scores) and the psychosocial factors (academic motivation, self-esteem, academic self-efficacy, perceived stress, academic adjustment, and perceived social support) predict first-year students' Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). To this end, correlational research design was employed. Data were gathered using Academic Motivation Scale, Rosenberg Self-esteem Scale, Academic Self-Efficacy Scale, Perceived Stress Scale, Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support Scale, Academic Adjustment Scale, Ethiopian University Entrance Examination, Secondary School GPA, and First-year CGPA. The research involved 343 first-year regular students of Wallaga University. Results revealed that academic motivation (r =.686; p < .001), self-esteem (r =.849; p < .001), academic adjustment (r =.771; p < .001), secondary school CGPA (r =.643; p < .001), and EUEE (r = .266; p < .001) were correlated positively and significantly with first-year students' CGPA, while perceived stress (r= -.164; p = .002) is negatively correlated with academic achievement. Moreover, self-esteem (beta = .539; p < .01), secondary school CGPA (beta =.232; p < .01), academic adjustment (beta =.219; p < .01), and academic self-efficacy (beta = -.075; p < .01) were found to be the significant predictors of first-year students' CGPA. Demographic variables, such as students' sex, the place where they grew up, and parents' level of education were also shown to be important determinant factors influencing students' academic success i.e. being male, being grew up in urban settings, and being from parents with higher educational status were important contributors for students' academic achievement. It is recommended that university leaders and instructors should provide the necessary support for their students' psychosocial adjustment by reducing their stress levels and thereby improve their CGPA. Studying psychosocial factors alongside prior academic performance factors is crucial because it provides a more holistic understanding of student success and failure. Thus, in the context of the Ethiopian higher education, where dropout rates remain a significant concern, this research offers valuable empirical evidence to inform institutional practices and policy interventions aimed at enhancing student retention and academic outcomes.

TI Student perception of opportunity competence development in mathematics:
   is it a unidimensional or multidimensional construct?
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Opportunity competence development; replicability of factors;
   mathematics education; item factor analysis; SPOCD questionnaire
ID MULTIPLE REPLICATION; COEFFICIENT ALPHA; FIT INDEXES; REGRESSION;
   INVENTORY; SCORE; DIF
AB This study aims to replicate the original factor structure of the Student Perception of Opportunity Competence Development (SPOCD) questionnaire and perform a model comparison using item factor analysis (IFA). The Indonesian SPOCD was administered to 594 high school students (255 males, 339 females) in the Jakarta metropolitan area of Indonesia. The results of the IFA showed that the higher-order multidimensional factor model of the SPOCD was acceptable and replicated the original model. Based on a statistical model comparison, we found the higher-order multidimensional model was superior to the unidimensional model. Moreover, each subscale of the SPOCD demonstrated good internal consistency, with omega coefficients of 0.720 to 0.800, and the total scale demonstrated good reliability, with an omega coefficient of 0.892. Thus, the Indonesian SPOCD questionnaire with higher-order multidimensional models appears to be a valid and reliable tool for assessing student perceptions of opportunity competence development in mathematics. Finally, separate scores for each SPOCD aspect can be used for diagnostic purposes in learning and has implications for the practice of mathematics teaching. Teachers can also use SPOCD scores as input for improving or maintaining aspects of opportunity competence development in their classes.

TI Quality of life and associated predictors in Palestinian medical
   students: a cross-sectional study
SO MEDICAL EDUCATION ONLINE
LA English
DT Article
DE Quality of life; medical students; social relationships; psychological
   well-being; physical health; preclinical phase; clinical phase
ID STRESS-MANAGEMENT; DEPRESSION; PREVALENCE; ANXIETY; HEALTH; US
AB Medical students experience tremendous stressors related to the demanding nature of medical education programs, which can negatively impact their health and overall quality of life (QoL). This particular study aimed to evaluate the QoL of medical students at Al-Quds University (AQU) in Palestine across various academic years and demographic variables, concerning physical health, psychological well-being, social relationships, and environmental conditions. A cross-sectional comparative study involving 522 medical students representing all six academic years was conducted from May to July 2024. QoL was assessed via the culturally adapted Arabic version of the World Health Organization Quality of Life (WHOQOL-BREF) questionnaire. Demographic variables (gender, age, place of residence, number of bedrooms) and academic (academic year) variables were examined as correlates of QoL domains. Descriptive statistics, independent t-tests, and one-way ANOVA were applied, and linear regression was used to identify predictors. A p-value of <= 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Social relationships were the highest-rated domain (M = 3.58, SD = 0.862), followed by physical health (M = 3.38, SD = 0.721), environment (M = 3.28, SD = 0.638), and psychological conditions (M = 3.12, SD = 0.693). Gender differences emerged, with males reporting better physical health (p = 0.002). Linear regression further identified academic level as a key predictor of physical health (p < 0.001). Medical students at AQU have shown resilience in their social relationships. However, concerns arise from their lower psychological health and limited access to recreational opportunities. These findings highlight the importance of targeted institutional strategies that address mental health and foster supportive environments. Ultimately, this approach aims to enhance student well-being and create a more balanced and sustainable quality of life for students.

TI Financial self-efficacy in aspiring entrepreneurs in Ghana: the
   moderating role of financial risk tolerance in predicting
   entrepreneurial intentions of university students
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Entrepreneurial intention; financial self-efficacy; financial risk
   tolerance; Ghanaian university students; PLS-SEM; General Psychology;
   Finance; Higher Education
ID ATTITUDES; MODELS; IMPACT
AB In emerging economies like Ghana, fostering entrepreneurship is crucial for economic development, yet the understanding of psychological factors influencing entrepreneurial intention (EI) remains underexplored. Addressing this gap, our research specifically probes the effects of financial self-efficacy (FSE) and financial risk tolerance (FRT) on EI among university students in Ghana. The study also explores the moderating effect of FRT in the FSE-EI relationship. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from 658 university students across private and public Ghanaian universities. PLS-structural equation modelling was used to examine the hypothesised relationships among FSE, FRT and EI. The results demonstrate that both FSE and FRT have significant positive effects on EI. Further, FRT significantly moderates the FSE-EI nexus. The findings offer valuable implications for educators, policymakers and entrepreneurship development programmes, suggesting the need to enhance financial self-efficacy and risk tolerance to cultivate EIs among potential entrepreneurs. The study extends the current understanding of EI by exploring the influence of FSE and FRT, contributing to the literature on the antecedents of EI. The focus on Ghanaian university students adds value to the discourse by providing empirical evidence from a less-examined context. Thus, this study provides actionable insights for entrepreneurship educators, policymakers, and training institutions in Ghana and similar emerging economies.

   three-component model
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article

   curriculum development; higher education
ID LECTURES; THINKING
AB This article presents a three-component model for teaching sustainable development in business education. It responds to a recognized curricular gap in how sustainable development is taught, particularly in U.S. undergraduate business programs. The model was implemented in introductory business courses at a U.S. university. The visual teaching framework, the ANSI University Outreach Program, and the ISO 26000:2010 guidance standard work together to deliver a cohesive learning experience focused on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) core subjects and sustainable development. The model led to improvements in student engagement, understanding, and application of sustainability concepts. This model contributes to sustainability-focused education and can be used by other instructors to meet learning goals related to ESG. In this way, the work has potentially vital implications in terms of ensuring that sustainable development receives more focus in the future, which can only benefit society and the environment while also ensuring that companies act in socially and environmentally responsible ways.

TI The Big-Fish-Little-Pond effect on mathematics students' intelligence
   mindset in selective and non-selective schools
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Big-Fish-Little-Pond Effect; growth mindset; selective schools; academic
   self-concept; mathematics education; fixed mindset; Social sciences;
   Behavioral sciences; Behavioral neuroscience; Cognitive neuroscience;
   Cognitive neuroscience of language; Developmental psychology; Language
   development; Infancy
ID ACADEMIC SELF-CONCEPT; ATTRIBUTION THEORY; IMPLICIT THEORIES; GROWTH
   MINDSET; FIT INDEXES; ACHIEVEMENT; MOTIVATION; SYSTEMS; VALUES
AB This study investigated the Big-Fish-Little-Pond Effect (BFLPE) on the intelligence mindset of mathematics students in selective and non-selective schools. The BFLPE framework posits that in highly competitive academic environments, students' self-concept may decline when surrounded by equally or more competent peers.The sample consisted of 362 upper secondary students (43.6% girls, 56.4% boys) from selective schools and non-selective schools . Data were collected using a mindset scale and analyzed with Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) to account for the nested structure of the data. The results showed that students in non-selective schools exhibited higher growth mindset scores compared to those in selective schools. These findings support the BFLPE, suggesting that selective schools may foster fixed mindsets due to their competitive environments. This research contributes to educational psychology by extending the BFLPE to a new cultural context where familial support is prominent and applying it to a different psychological construct-mindset theory.

TI Development of young children's origami skills: fine motor skills and
   spatial skills in making origami cicada
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Origami; fine motor skills; spatial skills; children's development;
   Developmental Psychology; Educational Psychology; Psychological Science;
   Childhood; Early Years
ID EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS; VISUOMOTOR INTEGRATION; PRESCHOOLERS; DIVERSITY;
   UNITY
AB Although origami has attracted the attention of educators regarding its possible application in educational settings, the specific abilities required for young children to successfully create origami works remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate how children develop precise folding skills, the impact of verbal prompts on folding, and the skills necessary to create origami works. Preschool-aged children completed tasks involving precise folding, making cicadas, figure recognition, and a hand game, which is an executive function task. Precise folding was indexed by the deviation of the folding, that is, the misalignment distance in the folding precision task. Cicada-making skills were assessed based on the amount of intervention required to perform each step of the task. Data analysis revealed that precise folding skills significantly improved around age four, suggesting that verbal guidance can enhance attention and hand movements. Hierarchical multiple regression showed that cicada-making skills were predicted by precise folding and figure recognition ability, independent of the individual's age. By providing empirical evidence on the components and development of children's origami skills, this study contributes to designing and promoting educational programs that utilize origami activities.

TI Effects of market forces on the academic performance of students with
   disabilities in public secondary schools in Kamuli municipality
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Students; disabilities; academic performance; secondary school;
   Inclusion and Special Educational Needs; Secondary Education; Education
   - Social Sciences
ID HIGHER-EDUCATION; VOICE
AB This qualitative exploratory study assessed the implications of market forces on the academic performance of students with disabilities in public secondary schools in Kamuli Municipality. Specifically, the availability and accessibility of instructional materials influence the academic performance of students with disabilities, the availability of competent teachers on the academic performance of students with disabilities, and the influence of external support from different stakeholders on the academic performance of students with disabilities. Using Interviews, responses from teachers and selected students were acquired. Findings indicate that access to instructional materials, assistive technology, and individualised education programs significantly improve academic performance for students with special needs. External forces, such as government and parental partnerships, play a crucial role in providing these resources and training teachers. Schools should foster collaboration among teachers, parents, and students to implement individualised education programs. Investing in teacher training, resources, and partnerships with external organisations can create an inclusive environment. The study concluded that market forces, specifically instructional materials, competent human resources, and external support, have a significant influence on the academic performance of students with disabilities. The study recommends that stakeholders should work towards ensuring that students with disabilities in secondary schools study in a conducive environment.

TI Elevating minds: how PISA-inspired enrichment fuels the motivation of
   gifted and high-achieving students in mathematics
SO COGENT EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Enrichment program; motivation to learn mathematics; intrinsic
   motivation; extrinsic motivation; contextual problems; United Arab
   Emirates; Inclusion and Special Educational Needs; Secondary Education;
   Education - Social Sciences
ID WORD-PROBLEMS; STRATEGIES; EDUCATION
AB Concern over pupils' lack of interest in mathematics is growing. In the past, bright and high performers in mathematics received little attention while the focus was on researching low achievers. Thus, this study aimed to determine how a mathematical literacy program affected the drive of talented and accomplished students to learn mathematics. This study used non-equivalent pre- and post-tests in a quasi-experimental research design. 102 advanced stream tenth-grade students from two public high schools in Al Ain, United Arab Emirates (UAE), participated in a motivation survey. The experimental and control groups' motivation to learn mathematics results showed strong levels of extrinsic and intrinsic drive. However, the students' extrinsic motivation in the experimental group improved after the implementation of the Mathematical Enrichment Program (MEP), while both intrinsic and extrinsic motivation improved significantly among the students in the control group. Male students were slightly more motivated than female students, but the two groups had no statistically significant differences. The findings' pedagogical and policy ramifications have been examined in the conclusion.
